title: Cling to God alone; love with whole soul; after courage, foundations
english: ON ADORATION AND WORSHIP IN SPIRIT AND TRUTH — BOOK SIX. That we must cling to God alone who is God by nature, and love him from whole soul and heart.

Cyril: Concerning the manliness understood in Christ, then, and spiritual good-strength, a sufficient word has been worked out by us, as it seems, Palladius; yet the things upon which these would come to be from our side it is necessary to look around at, as I think, again.
Palladius: You speak well.
Cyril: Come then already, turning the eye of the mind round in a circle, and going unto exact examination (Deuteronomy 6:5) (Mark 12:30)

title: Faith the foundation; first commandment; jealous God
english: of the things that concern us, let us look well which path going along we shall be bright, and shall bind on ourselves as it were some crown the vote upon all the things praised. Or do I not seem to you to think rightly, having chosen to be curious in these things at least?

Palladius: Altogether so. For I myself also would say that one must be whetted beforehand by the challenge toward manliness, and choose the things through which someone would be bright, and would come straight toward the blameless life.

Cyril: Therefore let us already say that of every house the support is a foundation; and of a temple the keel is a beginning; and of the one who has chosen to set things right, a foundation and beginning of a base would be the knowledge of the truth, and the unadulterated word concerning faith into the one God who is by nature and true: ‘For if you do not believe, you will not even understand,’ (Isaiah 7:9) says the sacred Letter. And those understanding must not yet be idle of the necessary things, not knowing how to set right. Or would you not say it is necessary toward our being well-approved, the examination upon every thing to be done, if we have made in word the doing rightly what it is necessary to love?
Palladius: I say so.

Cyril: Faith therefore is nurse of understanding. And understanding makes the testing of the things to be done for us. And indeed when the God of all set over those from Israel as it were some pedagogue and wise director—the law through Moses—he laid down beforehand as it were some base and unshaken beginning the knowledge from the one and true Godhead; for he supposed they would not be strong enough to reach the blameless and pure life, or to be rhythm-trained by the introducer of the finest things—the law—and to yield to commandments, unless having taken the faith upon God into mind as a fore-wall they should nobly stand against the pleasures that whet them unto slackness. It was necessary then, necessary, that those of old lay aside beforehand as it were some soul-sickness the polytheist wandering, and be well fixed by the faith into the one God by nature and truly; therefore also first a law shone forth to them: ‘I am the Lord your God, who led you out from Egypt’ (Exodus 20:2–6)s land from a house of slavery. There will not be for you other gods besides me. You will not make for yourself an idol, nor likeness of anything as many as are in the heaven above, and in the earth below, and as many as are in the waters under the earth; you will not worship them, nor will you serve them. For I am the Lord your God, a jealous God, paying back fathers’ sins upon children unto a third and fourth generation to those who hate me; and doing mercy unto thousands to those who love me and keep my ordinances.’ For it was necessary, necessary, that those about to make the commandment unmovable be terrified with hard fears; therefore he also names himself a jealous God, and one who lays fathers’ sins upon those from them, if indeed they should choose to live according to those ones, and (Deuteronomy 5:6–10)

title: Fathers’ sins; vain Name; idols; Trinity without polytheism
english: to race with ancestral stumblings. For we do not say somewhere that fathers’ sins strike down upon those who have altogether done nothing wrong, although God has cried out expressly: ‘Fathers will not die on behalf of children, nor children on behalf of fathers; each will die in his own sin.’ (Deuteronomy 24:16) Yet if those from them should follow the fathers’ judgments, and be zealots of ancestral impiety, the wrath somehow stretches even unto them. And even if somehow from inborn love-of-humanity the God above all should let go the first ones from needing to be punished, yet late he brings upon the second or the third the anger fitting and owed at the beginnings to the profane race. He was therefore frightening them unto needing to fear, naming himself a jealous God; yet he was also confirming them otherwise unto faith, promising to do mercy unto thousands to those who love him. And he was adding to these a neighboring and sister commandment: ‘For you will not take,’ he says, ‘the name of the Lord your God upon a vain thing; for the Lord will not cleanse the one taking his name upon a vain thing.’ (Exodus 20:7) Some were doing this, fastening the calling of God upon woods and stones, and unlearnedly bringing down the name above every name unto a handiwork and toil of a human hand. And God said somewhere concerning them through Isaiah’s voice: ‘A craftsman choosing a wood stood it in a measure, and in glue shaped it, and made it as a form of a man, and as beauty of a human to stand it in a house; he cut wood from the thicket which the Lord planted, and rain lengthened it, that it might be for humans unto burning, and taking from it he was warmed, and having burned they baked breads upon them; yet the remainder they worked into gods, and they worship them.’ (Isaiah 44:13–20) And after other things: ‘Know that their heart is ash, and they wander.’ (1 Corinthians 8:5–6) These take the Lord’s name upon a vain thing. Yet I think those who have already come to be outside a diabolic snare, and have known the true God, must not kneel unto cold thoughts, nor honor the ignoble in this at least with empty talk, being dragged opposite unto needing to know other gods, or to think that any exist at all beside the one and truly. ‘For even if some are called gods and lords, both in heaven and upon earth, yet for us one God, the Father, from whom are all things and we unto him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, through whom are all things, and we through him; and one Holy Spirit, in whom are all things, and we in him.’ (Deuteronomy 6:13) For we least of all contract the nature of the Godhead in a Jewish way unto only the one God and Father, yet widening as it were unto a holy and consubstantial Trinity; and indeed also distinguishing by quality of persons and property of hypostasis, we contract again unto one God, because of the sameness of substance, and we will serve him, we will worship him, calling upon the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit. ‘For there will not be,’ he says, ‘other gods besides me;’ and again: ‘The Lord your God you will wor

title: One God; no limping both ways; no second baptism after apostasy
english: ship, and him alone you will serve.’ And since there is one God the Father, and one Lord the Son, and one Holy Spirit proceeding, we will neither carry out the one God from true lordship; nor indeed will we send out the one who is truly and by nature Lord from being God; for lordship will altogether follow the Godhead according to nature; and again to lordship according to truth, the glory of the Godhead.
Palladius: Most rightly and most wisely you have spoken.

Cyril: One God therefore, Palladius, we will know, and upon him we will count no one at all, making the unholy and profane double-souledness, as boastful and truly insolent, farthest from our own soul, in order that a sacred word may not also cry out upon us ourselves: ‘How long will you limp upon both hams? either Baal Baal, or God God.’ (Deuteronomy 6:13) For we must be seen single-turned, not other-minded and shaken, falling most ready into what is not fitting; as for limping upon both and loving to be tossed, I would say it is of the most godless things. And indeed the ancient law also honors with death the one not secure, for it says: ‘The one sacrificing to gods will be wiped out, except to the Lord alone.’ (1 Kings 18:21) Therefore to lift oneself against the divine glory, and to distribute the things fitting it and it alone to whomever someone might choose, and to favor with them those not gods by nature, would be a most shameful of sicknesses, or rather an accusation and indictment of the last impiety. It is necessary therefore to have been freed from such things, the one at least who is truly genuine and God-loving, and not only cleansing the heart, but not even so much as to say ever sending through the tongue the idol name. For it has been written that ‘And you will not remember a name of other gods, nor will it be heard from your mouth.’ (Exodus 22:20) For what it is shameful to know, it is not without penalty to speak. And having chosen to honor the genuine in faith everywhere, it is fitting to remember blessed Paul writing thus: ‘For it is impossible that those once enlightened, and having tasted a good utterance of God, and powers of a coming age, and having fallen aside, be renewed again unto repentance.’ (Exodus 23:13) For those once brought unto partaking of the heavenly and divine grace through the holy baptism, and having received the true and life-giving word concerning resurrection and Christ’s kingdom, if they should choose to run back toward what was at the beginnings, and to run under the first sickness, they will not be renewed toward cleansing through a second baptism; ‘For their unbelief will not abolish God’ (Hebrews 6:4–6)s faith,’ as divine Paul says. Nor because some have despised going backward the divine grace will we write down the insecure; yet rather the Judge of all will subject to penalties those not declining to slide down unto this impiety, as having trampled the Son of God and counted the blood of the covenant common, and having insulted the Spirit of grace, in whom (Romans 3:3) (Hebrews 10:29)

title: Destroy idols after Jordan; bless bread/wine/water as mysteries
english: they were sanctified, and have become sharers of the divine nature. For just as a soldier who has thrown away the shield and fled the war must not be honored with second sealings, but already be punished, and pay accounts of unmanliness; in the same manner, I think, those so insulting a reverend and admirable grace must not be honored with a second gift of the Spirit, the first having been set aside, but already it is fitting they lie under penalties. For that those once enlightened must come unto this judgment and steadiness of reasonings—to know one God by nature, and to abominate those introducing something other beside this, and to make finest of desires the leaping upon idols, and shaking down temples, and counting the Greeks’ worships nothing—an ancient word will also teach us. For it has been written in Numbers: ‘And the Lord spoke toward Moses on the west of Moab beside the Jordan opposite Jericho, saying: Speak to the sons of Israel, and you will say toward them: You are crossing the Jordan into Canaan’ (2 Peter 1:4)s land, and you will destroy all who dwell in the land before your face. And you will lift out their lookouts, and all their cast idols you will destroy them, and all their steles you will lift out.’ You understand that those who have passed the Jordan must make altars and precincts from the midst, and pry up without care the idols themselves and steles? as for allotting sparing perhaps to such evils, it would become a clear indication of not having been fixed well, nor dedicating the heart unaccused to God, although he says clearly concerning the godless and evil: ‘You will not worship their gods, nor will you serve according to their works, but with a taking-down you will take down, and crushing you will crush their steles, and you will serve the Lord your God, and I will bless your bread, and your wine, and your water; and I will turn weakness away from you; there will not be barren, nor sterile upon your land; I will fill up the number of your days.’ (Numbers 33:50–52) For it is not unclear that for those very well fixed and from a healthy mind clinging to the God of all, and having practiced to make a clear demonstration of the matter—the shaking down of altars and steles, and playthings of humans corrupted in mind—it will be a procurer of divine gifts.
Palladius: True.

Cyril: For if indeed you should take down the hand-made things, he says, and should serve God, having hated the customs beside those ones, ‘I will bless your bread, and your wine, and your water.’ (Exodus 23:24–26) The word is mystical and deep; for for those genuine toward God, the partaking of Christ’s mysteries will be unto spiritual blessing, and the grace through the holy baptism. Yet for those still double-souled, moved unto apostasy, wrath and condemnation; and what of the terrible things is the sharing of the spiritual blessing not? and this, (1 Corinthians 10:16)

title: Worthy Eucharist; smash high places; do not copy nations’ rites
english: I think, is what wise Paul also said, that ‘The one eating and drinking the body and blood of Christ unworthily eats and drinks judgment to himself, not discerning the Lord’ (1 Corinthians 11:27–28)s body. Yet let a human test himself,’ he says, ‘and then eat from the bread, and drink from the cup;’ (Deuteronomy 12:1–3) The partaking of the holy mysteries will therefore be unto blessing, he says, for those at least who are truly most God-loving. And they will be freed from softening—that is, from being ready to be sick with what is by nature unjust, and carrying off unto unmanliness; yet neither will there be barren among them, he says, nor sterile. For every God-loving and holy soul is most fertile, and leafy with holy fruits—I mean again the boasts from virtue.
Palladius: So it is.

Cyril: And not allowing to have the heart easy to shake, he skillfully turns us toward needing to choose what stands firm unto faith, and securely unto piety; for sometimes educating by fitting reasonings unto the better, he commands to be eager away from—or rather to turn away altogether, as procurer of ruin—the sacrificing to idols or worshiping, showing such a sickness full of the last slander, or rather of the highest impiety; and sometimes also setting fear—I mean that of being punished—as it were some pedagogue and noble guard for us, he turns us from every side unto what pleases him. And indeed in Deuteronomy blessed Moses says: ‘And these are the ordinances and the judgments which you will keep to do upon the land which the Lord the God of your fathers gives you in a lot all the days which you live upon the earth. With destruction you will destroy all the places in which the nations served their gods there, whom you inherit, upon the high mountains, and upon the dunes, and under a leafy tree. And you will dig down their altars, and smash their steles, and cut out their groves, and the carved things of their gods you will burn with fire, and you will destroy their name from that place.’ (Deuteronomy 12:29–30) The wise and select of Greeks, and poets especially, name some mountain-nymphs and tree-nymphs, or demons. And there are those who having chosen to honor the gods beside themselves with the heights according to place, setting altars on mountains, were eager to sacrifice oxen, and having settled around the more well-grown of the trees groves and images of demons, were using sheep-slaughters. Yet it was necessary that those come to be under God who is according to truth and by nature, dreading nothing, shake down the playthings of the wanderers, and go as far as possible from the customs beside those ones. Therefore he says again: ‘And if the Lord your God should wipe out the nations unto whom you go there to inherit their land, from your face, and you should inherit them, and settle in their land, take heed to yourself, lest you seek to follow along with them after they have been wiped out from your face; you will not seek their gods, saying, How do these nations do to their

title: No child-sacrifice; false prophet dies; God tests love
english: gods, I will also do; you will not do thus to the Lord your God; for the abominations which the Lord hated they did to their gods, because they also burn their sons and their daughters in fire to their gods.’ Well does the lawgiver forbid altogether the imitation of the wanderers, and very well commands to stand off from the merciless slaughter of children. And he convicts as destroyers and ruiners of humanity the blood-loving and falsely-named gods, who even savagely dishonor the laws of necessary affection, for the sake of what seems good to them; ‘For God created the all unto being, and the generations of the world are saving, and there is not a kingdom of Hades upon earth. Yet by envy of a devil death entered into the world.’ (Deuteronomy 12:30–31) And the divine will overturns death, and dissolves corruption; and hates that the things that are should not be; for he created the all unto being, according as it has been written. Yet those netted unto wandering by the demons’ greediness bring forward to Satan as it were seasonings, and of the most useful and sweet-smelling incense, the destruction of those come to be unto life, and the death of those created unto being. Most skillfully therefore he wished to show that the customs beside those ones are full of the last slander, and nature being wronged, and the ordinances of much-prayed-for love-of-children being trampled, very well hustling the noble and evil-hating mind of the hearers unto needing to honor and choose swiftly whatever he himself would wish and say. And these things were legislated of old unto overturning of the unholiness beside those ones. Yet he also defines death for the one wishing to persuade away the one who has been fixed, and who has received in a God-loving way the knowledge of the truth. For he said thus again: ‘And if a prophet should rise among you or a dreamer of a dream, and should give you a sign or wonder, and the sign or the wonder should come which he spoke toward you, saying: Let us go and serve other gods whom you have not known, you will not hear the words of that prophet or of that dreamer of that dream, because the Lord your God is testing you to know whether you love your God from your whole heart, and from your whole soul; behind the Lord your God you will go, and him you will fear, and his commandments you will keep, and his voice you will hear, and him you will serve, and to him you will be added. And that prophet or that dreamer of the dream will die; for he spoke to make you wander away from the Lord your God.’ (Wisdom 1:13–14) How holy and fitting to God the law! For if indeed for murderers of bodies death must follow altogether and in every way according to laws, how would the one bringing the ruinous wandering upon a soul, and casting the better than body into pits of destruction, according to the Savior’s own voice, not reasonably be in danger? title: Death for apostasy; love God above kin; broken cisterns
english: and he votes the equal penalty also upon the easily-carried and light mind of those subjected to such things. For when it was possible easily to flee, he says, waking up toward the true, for what did he make the voluntary running-off unto what wrongs? ‘And if there should be found among you in one of your cities which the Lord your God gives you, a man or woman who will do the evil opposite the Lord your God, to pass by his covenant, and going away they should serve other gods, and worship them—the sun or the moon, or any of those from the cosmos of the heaven, which he did not command you—and it was not announced to you, and you will seek very much, and behold the word has become true, this abomination has come to be in Israel; and you will lead out that human, or that woman, who did this evil deed, and you will stone them with stones, and they will die; upon two witnesses or upon three witnesses the one dying will die; he will not die upon one witness; and the hand of the witnesses will be upon him first to put him to death, and the hand of all the people at the last; and you will lift out the evil from yourselves;’ (Deuteronomy 17:2–7) For when God has been wronged concerning his own worship, to pity is not secure. And altogether harmful is not to be soft at the right time toward unmanly mutual-affections; and this, I think, is what the Lord said: ‘The one loving father or mother above me is not worthy of me.’ (Matthew 10:37) For let even then a law of affection go away, and let a power of natural love depart, and every thing whatever of the things coming unto love-of-humanity, and that we may speak thus, let God be served through a pious hardness. Or do you not say it is holy that those having unexcused the apostasy must be punished without pity, as grieving the glory beyond all, and not declining to insult without guard him whom it was somehow better to gladden with eagernesses unto steadfastness?
Palladius: Holy—for how not?

Cyril: And I will remember him saying through to those more ancient: ‘What wrong did your fathers find in me, that they stood away from me far, and went behind the vain things, and were made vain?’ (Jeremiah 2:5) And as it were astonished at the undiluted unlearnings of those from Israel, he says somehow thus: ‘Heaven was astonished upon this, and the earth shuddered still more very much, says the Lord; because my people did two evil things. Me they left—a spring of living water—and they dug for themselves crushed cisterns, which will not be able to hold water.’ (Jeremiah 2:12–13) For I would think, and very reasonably, that those standing off from the worship unto God, serving the creation beside the Creator and Maker, or still leaping down toward a more shameful wandering, worshiping the works of their own hands, miss every good-counsel; although it was easy, if indeed they should choose to think rightly, to look down upon the beauty of the nature above all and unspeakable from the creation of a world, and from the good-order of the things come to be to understand the orderer and leader and craftsman of this all. title: Wood ‘father’; fake piety; God near sees all
english: more ancient exchanged golden things for bronze, according to the poets beside Greeks. For having let go the needing to worship God who is according to nature, they turned childishly toward useless random-worship; pouring shame and laughter upon their own head, and having chosen a self-called falling-away from the help from above. And indeed God said: ‘As a thief’s shame when he is caught, so will the sons of Israel themselves be shamed, and their kings, and their rulers, and their priests, and their prophets; to the wood they said, You are my father, and to the stone: You begot me. And they turned backs upon me, and not their faces; and in the time of their evils they will say: Rise and save us. And where are your gods, whom you made for yourself? If they will rise and save you in the time of your ill-treatment? because according to the number of your cities were your gods, Judah, and according to the number of Jerusalem’s ways they were sacrificing to Baal. Why do you speak toward me? All you have lawlessly acted unto me, says the Lord.’
Palladius: Terrible truly is the matter, friend.

Cyril: Yet someone sometimes of those finishing among us, not yet very much fixed, yet having practiced a plastered and bastard love unto Christ, and such as putting around himself as it were a fleece the seeming to be God-loving, will be a bitter and unholy beast, both a monkey and facing-both-ways, so as at home and by night—I mean the having-escaped-notice—to cling to the demons’ worships, and somehow to think reasonably that he himself also can run past God, and out-reason the mind of the unspeakable nature. And one would show even very without-toil that the one for whom these things are present to think has chosen the more shameful things of the Greeks’ silliness. For to the wise beside Greeks it seemed to hold rightly that the sun, being created and begotten—the great light-bearer, and made upon this very thing from beside God—sees all and hears all; for they thought that what has been taken along in a God’s rank must be rich with the dignities of the divine nature. And a dignity of the highest nature is to know and look down upon the all. Yet those ones in these things; and to us God was calling of old: ‘I am a God drawing near, says the Lord, and not a God from far; will anything be hidden from me?’ (Jeremiah 2:26–29) For nothing would escape the one who is truly God by nature. And let blessed David mystagogue saying: ‘Understand already, senseless ones among the people, and fools, sometime be thoughtful; the one who planted the ear, will he not hear? and the one who shaped eyes, will he not understand?’ (Jeremiah 23:23–24) Some were saying, I think, from ununderstanding: ‘The Lord will not see, nor will the God of Jacob understand.’ (Psalm 94:8–9) Or is it not altogether silly to say that the supplier of knowledge neither knows, nor to think that the one giving the matter to those come to be from beside him does not hear (Psalm 94:7)?

title: Worship God alone; no omens; hear the prophet like Moses—Christ
english: Palladius: Altogether unpersuasive.

Cyril: One must therefore worship the Lord God alone and whole-turned, according to the Scriptures, and no one other beside him. For it has been written that ‘You will be perfect opposite the Lord your God.’ (Deuteronomy 18:9–15) And spiritual perfectness is the being settled in faith, and blameless unto worship, and the unaccused beauty of the love unto God.
Palladius: So I say.

Cyril: Therefore, Palladius, those who have least chosen to worship other gods, or the creation beside the one who created—yet somehow being persuaded by the false-prophecies of the idol-servers—will we free from blame and accusation? or safely show free of the charges unto apostasy to those at least who are truly genuine?
Palladius: Not at all.

Cyril: And star-sorceries and omen-takings and false-prophecies, and demonic trickings, would fit, I think somewhere, only and perhaps those who have most outlandishly been eager to settle into mind the inglorious and cursed idolatry.

Palladius: You have spoken rightly. Since indeed a divine word also charges us that we must abominate the shamefulness unto these at least. And it holds thus: ‘And if you should enter into the land which the Lord your God gives you, you will not learn to do according to the abominations of those nations; there will not be found in you one purifying his son and his daughter in fire, one prophesying a prophecy, and taking omens, and observing birds, a sorcerer, singing a charm, a ventriloquist, and wonder-watcher, and asking the dead; for every one doing these is an abomination to the Lord your God.’ (Deuteronomy 18:13) And after other things again he says: ‘You will be perfect before the Lord your God; these nations, whom you will inherit them, these will hear omen-takings and prophecies; yet not thus has the Lord your God given to you. A prophet from your brothers like me the Lord your God will raise; [him you will hear according to all as many as you asked from beside the Lord your God] at Horeb on the day of the assembly.’ (Acts 3:22)

Cyril: Well done, friend. For we will follow not wonder-watchers and dead-diviners, nor will we receive flights of birds as some true matter, even if they should be borne toward the right, or then unto the left; even if toward evening and toward dawn; for these things are of the last folly. Yet making Christ the prophet for us and among us the leader of the all, from him we will take the knowledge of the necessary things, and we will sit beside him, saying a long wail to the demons’ false-speakings and ‘farewell.’ For to God alone as it were will the needing to make-alive and to rule the all be laid down naturally and specially (John 6:14);

Cyril: Well done, Palladius. And I would still wish us looking around well at the true also to examine this: in what manner still, if we finish at all among those wishing to live rightly and evangelically, will we follow the flatteries of false-prophecies and indeed also, having attended as if some word from beside them were true, not mark off the Savior’s voice as needing to be false? title: Burial Phoebizing; true cleansing Christ Spirit baptism

The divine oracle therefore bars us from such shameful and most unbeautiful practices. For it is not at all fitting to count the death of bodies a pollution of soul, nor indeed to think that the sight upon a dead one impresses filth upon the hearts of those seeing, nor again upon this is it fitting to strip the hair. For the matter is altogether stale and full of the ground-crawling glory. Well then the law says the ‘You will not Phoebize;’ (Isaiah 43:25) for such a cleansing will not benefit a soul, yet rather does injustice, both taking away the knowledge of the most beneficial path, and carrying away from the hunt of the advantageous. For let us look thus: Laws beside us of those ruling upon earth are, awarding and refusing the things to be done and not to those everywhere; yet no one would be able to flee the justices upon the transgressions, unless needing to be let go from the king’s mildness granting it to him. In the equal manner then, the one having disregarded the divine laws would not become clean, unless having become rich with the matter by a divine nod. For if we have transgressed laws of fire or water, and the account of the sin looks unto those, let the water wash off the writing, let the fire melt down the filth, and letting go upon authority the charges to whomever they should choose; yet if true is the one saying toward God: ‘Against you alone I have sinned, and I have done the evil before you,’ (Deuteronomy 14:1) for one is the lawgiver and judge, instead of which having let go the lord of both punishing and letting go, they slide down into old-wives’ thoughts, distributing to fire and water the being able to free them from the charges. Away with the bad counsel, O human, approach the God alone according to nature, and you will hear him saying at once: ‘I am the one wiping out your lawlessnesses for my sake, and I will not remember.’ (Psalm 50:6 (LXX 50:6)) This is true cleansing; this is the spiritual brightness; for we have been wiped, having gained by the faith into Christ the forgiveness of the sin, yet having been made holy by the bath of regeneration, and having enriched ourselves with the divine grace, that of the divine Spirit, which also in the manner of fire consumes as some refuse the pollution that has settled into our understandings. For the God-breathed Scripture says thus justly that we have been baptized in Holy Spirit and fire.

title: Fate Fortune Genesis vs free will; Solon reductio
english: Cyril: Altogether so. For the matter is full of godlessness. And one would reasonably also range with these and number together the thinking that human things are administered by others’ nods, and that the authority of the things according to us has been hung not upon ourselves, but upon those whom the inventors of such unpersuasive doctrines should choose to myth-mold. For Fate and Fortune and Genesis, I do not know how, setting them as it were some steersmen over the life, they say each of us is not a willer or lord of the things to be done; yet to be led as from a necessary bond toward what seems to those ruling. Then what would ever become more irrational than such a thing? And how would Satan have done greater injustice to the race of humans, than when he disposed them to think and reason thus? For how would someone still counsel the useful things, and go willingly-working upon them ever? And having come to be also in the more shameful things, and having thought what one must not, how would he accuse himself and having melted with griefs change counsel to think and do the better things? For just as for those darting through the sea and having chosen to sail through there is somehow every necessity to be led by winds from the stern, and to be forced everywhere toward what seems to the pushing-together; so somewhere altogether also for us ourselves it is necessary to yield, unto whatever Fortune should choose to ferry, and the hard-to-flee winds of Fate according to them. Or will you yourself also think again that these things have been said rightly?
Palladius: For how not?
Cyril: Therefore it is altogether silly to crown the good and fair one with praises, and to count him worthy of honor, yet to count the wicked and unbridled one abominable and spat-upon.
Palladius: In what manner do you say?

title: Euripides: know good, not do; inequality under God
english: Already somehow otherwise in night’s long time I have thought of mortals, how life has been corrupted. And they seem to me not according to nature of judgment to practice worse; for the thinking well is for many. Do you understand how it does not seem to the more ancient ones to accuse Fortune, not Genesis, not Fate, as thrusting us out with force from the known uprightness, and from as many useful things as we should learn? title: Pray Lord Sabaoth yourself; James 5; no false oaths
english: mies. And you, if you ache in some of the body’s portions, and have truly believed that the Lord Sabaoth, and such callings which the divine Scripture distributes to the God according to nature, will become loosening for you of the evil, yourself praying on behalf of yourself, cry out the words; for you will do better than those, laying up the glory for God, and not for the unclean spirits. And I will also remember the God-breathed Scripture saying: ‘Is someone weak among you? Let him call the elders of the Church, and let them pray upon him, having anointed him with oil, in the name of the Lord; and the prayer of the faith will save the one laboring, and the Lord will raise him, and if he has done sins, it will be forgiven him.’ (James 5:14–15)

Palladius: Let bird-watching then, and indeed also charm, be ranged together, if it seems good, with those having been accused from law, and with those in most shameful and most abominable glory beside God.

Cyril: And very much, and I would add that also in other manners we will insult God, and someone would owe a writing and words of the impiety unto him, having chosen to false-swear, and to say some reverse-speaking and discordant thing against at least the highest and uppermost glory. For the one is punished with the altogether anger, and with unmanageable penalty, the sickle completing, according as it has been written, the false-swearer’s hearth, and shaking it down unto the complete: ‘For it will enter,’ (James 5:12) it says, ‘into the house of the thief, and into the house of the one swearing by my name upon a lie, and will dissolve in the middle of his house, and will complete him, and his woods, and his stones.’ (Zechariah 5:3–4) Yet the other—the needing to have died, and to have the justice beyond all the evils. Therefore one must swear not upon a lie; or rather not swear at all. For this the Savior taught us, saying: ‘Let your Yes be yes, and your No, no; and the excess of these is from the devil.’ (Matthew 5:37) For there will not be need of an oath at all for those in a reputation of solemnity, and having made virtue as it were house-mate; for among the lovers of piety the life of such ones has been very much honored, and to hate being disbelieved; and if somehow he should utter something, he is at once crowned with the hearers’ faith. Therefore let our life be well-glorious, and the need of swearing through will altogether somehow be idle, as I think. And if somehow it should come to be, and of some sometimes thinking little of the honor unto holy ones, let God be oath-partner, let another’s name of some not be carried beside. For already some going without looking-around unto loose fadings pretend to be indifferent, saying by heaven, or justice, by Adrasteia, by the light, by the lamp. And collecting some other things according to what seems to them, they somehow perhaps also think to be pious, thrusting aside the divine name, yet gilding with the glory fitting for God the things having been called unto genesis by his nods. Such a wandering we will find Israel having been sick with according to seasons. For confessedly to God they built up the one in Jerusalem (Zechariah 5:4)

title: Temple boast; heaven/earth oaths; Yes-Yes; greater than man
english: temple, and thinking great upon this very thing, and having believed they had come inside the boasts unto piety, and to take very well a most notable glory of the things announced to them through all-wise Moses, thinking little they were being caught carelessly; yet that the matter will not be for them unto good-fame from somewhere, and God does not delight in the buildings from stones, he was teaching saying: ‘The heaven is a throne for me, and the earth a footstool of my feet. What sort of house will you build for me? Or what place of my rest? says the Lord.’ (Isaiah 66:1) For God fills all things, and rests upon heaven, yet also reaches upon the earth; for the divine is not in quantity, but just as it is farthest from bodily fantasy, so also from place and from seeming to have been quantified. And since once Jews were hearing him saying, The heaven is a throne for me, and the earth a footstool of my feet, going unto unsafe thoughts, they were making the heaven an oath-partner, naming it a divine throne, and likewise also the earth, as lying under God’s feet; and indeed also Jerusalem, for it is a city, they were saying, of the God ruling all—although the more ancient holy ones had made the ‘The Lord lives’ (Exodus 22:10–11) in need of an oath. Yet the Savior counterfeited the Jews’ most silly thought, saying one must not swear off, neither in the heaven, because it is God’s throne, nor in the earth, because it is a footstool of his feet, nor unto Jerusalem, because it is a city of the great king; for what those ones were saying while babbling, these things the Savior uttered usefully, proving everywhere their piety in these things at least as plastered-on, and invented from I know not where. Therefore let the wandering upon this also be gone. For we have been taught in the needs of an oath never to have remembered any other at all, yet rather to make unto a safe and worthy faith the Yes, yes, and the No, no. And the law also said: ‘If a deposit should be destroyed toward someone, and the one having given should demand the faith upon this, there will be an oath of God in between both.’ (Matthew 5:34–37) And humans swear according to the greater; for thus Paul the wise said to us; and we say it is greater than a human, understanding rightly, not by size perhaps, or then excessing in understanding and wisdom and glory, but as the being somehow thus for us.
Palladius: I do not understand what you say.

Cyril: And indeed, O Palladius, clear, as at least it seems to me, and evident is the word. Or do we not say that many of the things made differ incomparably by size from human bodies, and besides the heaven?
Palladius: And very much.
Cyril: And in understanding and wisdom and thinness of bodies, do angels not excel?
Palladius: They excel, but also in honor.
Cyril: And in brightness and glory—I mean the one according to body—is not the sun’s nature incomparably better (Hebrews 6:16) (Matthew 5:34–35);
Palladius: Better.

title: Swear by God alone; blasphemy vs Spirit; no limping both
english: Cyril: It has been fixed then, that each of these would reasonably have as toward us the excelling, according to which it has been born to conquer. Will we then make these oath-partners, having left as superfluous the remembering of God?
Palladius: Not at all.
Cyril: Therefore then what is by nature overstretched and having differed by the whole being from the things made—that is, God—seems also to say greater than a human.
Palladius: You speak well.

Cyril: Therefore let the Yes, and the No, beside those having chosen to live best, be both need and power of an oath, and let it have been fixed rightly; for thus will also follow the needing to be believed. And if the Yes and the No should be dishonored by someone, let the need of the oaths be turned hereafter unto the greater than according to us, or rather than according to all the creation. And blasphemy—what would I say hereafter, where it is, and that it may carry off unto evil those using it—which the ancient law also honors with bitter death. And Christ himself has also condemned it with inescapable and endless evils: ‘For whoever should say a word against the Son of the human, it will be forgiven him; yet whoever should say against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven him, neither in the now age, nor in the coming.’ (Matthew 12:32) Calling Spirit the nature above body, which is God, to whom the one daring to send an unbridled tongue will reap the fruits of doorless-mouthing. ‘For lips of a fool lead him unto evils, according as it has been written. And his bold mouth calls upon death.’ (Psalm 141:3–4) Therefore also the divine Melodist was saying: ‘Set, Lord, a guard for my mouth, and a door of enclosure around my lips; do not lean my heart aside unto words of wickedness.’ (1 Kings 18:21) And these would be a most unholy shouting-down against God and the unspeakable and undefiled nature.
Palladius: One must then be well fixed, those hurrying to go blamelessly upon the straight, and not enduring to strike against God.

Cyril: Thus I say. For toward those approaching God not from a healthy heart, but from a suspected and corrupted one, and having chosen to be sick with the strengthless and easily-shaken, the prophet says: ‘Until when will you limp upon both your hams, either Baal, Baal, or God, God?’ (Proverbs 18:6–7) For the neither healthy altogether toward faith, nor indeed loving to have been fixed unto wandering, is to limp upon both, and indeed, what is upon each destroys the genuine. And a pretext of the thus rotten and easily-broken judgment would become for some, I think, the making plastered-on and not true the loving unto God, and to play-act wishing to Christianize, yet not to do this from whole heart, nor indeed having been persuaded by shame toward the true and having honored what holds rightly; but either hunting

title: Gibeonite hypocrisy; whole love; Book 6 Amen
english: what is according to pleasure for themselves, or a fear of danger, and a wild approach of ill-day, as it were bewitching, to seem to have come forward to the faith, in order that they may have many who have chosen to contend together, and to lend their own care. Yet a last care will be distributed to such ones, and the lot in the ones most especially cast down; and most dishonored and thrown-away and scarcely gaining the being counted worthy of life, they would be caught when God tests the things hidden in us—such as were those from Gibeon. For they once approached Joshua, and were very much begging to be made intimate with the people of God; yet they were not making the running-toward without evil-working, nor indeed simple and unadulterated, and as from love toward God, but in play-acting and deceit. And they escaped notice at the beginnings. But when being caught doing bitter things, and having been found out both ill-minded and many-judgmented, they were being set in the last things. For they have become both wood-cutters and water-carriers for all the Synagogue. Do you see then where the not-genuine will bring down, and the not having chosen to honor from a healthy understanding the spiritual intimacy toward holy ones. For sometimes some deceive—and I do not say the Christ who knows all, but rather those in his type, that is, those leading peoples. Just as indeed also those ones then brought Joshua into an image and under-type of Christ, and they drive in with deceit of shadowings, in depth of reasonings, and holding forward the play-acting of the wickedness unto mind; yet being condemned—for it is not possible to escape notice—they will be saved scarcely, having the slave-fitting and last portion; for of an unfree judgment, deceit is fruit. Yet we, for whom the aiming is to think healthily the things of God and the remaining things are unspelled, will cling to our own Master and God of the wholes, from a simple heart, from a right understanding, from a whole love, not enduring the double-souled to be sick, yet standing off altogether from Greek habits and thoughts, and going as farthest and very swiftly from the things having been condemned from law. For thus we will be perfect opposite the Lord God, according as it has been written, and bright, and well-approved with the other holy ones in Christ, through whom and with whom to the Father glory with Holy Spirit unto the ages of the ages. Amen (Deuteronomy 18:13) (James 1:8) (Matthew 5:48).
